stories.title: Agents are becoming a user group product designers have to design for
stories.blurb: Linear's CPO reports MCP usage going through the roof, framed in a roundup of six emerging UX and design trends with examples from Linear, Netflix, Runway, FullStory and Square. The question raised is whether agents are the next users designers plan interfaces around.

stories.title: How client work and deadlines quietly reshape a designer's stance on AI
stories.blurb: A first-person account of how years of commercial practice change the way designers relate to emerging technology. Less a position on AI than a look at the professional conditions that produce the position.

stories.title: Instagram's rebrand: a wordmark change and the system behind it
stories.blurb: Meta has given Instagram a reworked identity built to flex and grow. It's Nice That's long read with Meta's Jasmine Probst and May Hartono covers how the system was assembled across a large team and why the hardest work is the part nobody sees.

stories.title: Pentagram builds a dynamic identity for a concert hall inside a medieval hospital
stories.blurb: Muziekcentrum De Bijloke in Ghent occupies a hospital founded in 1251, with a 13th-century main hall. Pentagram's answer is a dynamic visual identity rather than a fixed mark.

stories.title: The tool shift argument, made by someone who has lived through several
stories.blurb: A practitioner traces the moves from ink pens to Macs, hand-drawn type to digital foundries, marker visuals to 3D renders, and argues the creative industry has always absorbed new tools. The claim under the headline is that happy accidents are the part that does not transfer.

stories.title: Gotham at 25 gets a variable axis
stories.blurb: Monotype is giving Gotham room to move with a variable version. Sara Soskolne's angle is how legacy identities absorb flexibility and new technology without losing what made them legible as identities.

stories.title: Why a Japanese potato chip bag lost its colour
stories.blurb: A packaging change read as a symptom: economic and political turbulence is resetting the defaults of Japanese design. Useful as a reminder that visual conventions have material causes.

stories.title: Amazon is buying rare books, scanning them and destroying them for training data
stories.blurb: A hidden AirTag traced the route. Rare print is valuable to model makers precisely because it was never online, which puts the acquisition of training corpora back in view as a physical, irreversible act.

stories.title: Stripe reportedly buying OpenRouter for more than $7B
stories.blurb: OpenRouter's CEO has described the company as Stripe for AI. If the deal lands, the layer most small teams use to reach several models at once sits with a payments company.

stories.title: Anthropic sets out how invisible watermarks in Claude text will work
stories.blurb: The mechanism is aimed at Europe's AI transparency rules and marks generated text rather than images. Anyone shipping written work through a model now has a provenance question attached to it.

stories.title: ChatGPT's desktop app starts recording how you work
stories.blurb: Computer History on macOS turns clicks and keystrokes into training data, learns your patterns, suggests automations and picks up tasks. For studio machines holding client material, that is a settings question, not a feature note.

stories.title: OpenAI disbanded its preparedness team
stories.blurb: Per the Financial Times, the group tasked with assessing serious model risks was dissolved at the end of last month. Responsibilities were not reported as replaced, only removed.
